explanation: A yellow slime mould spreads through every corridor, then pulls back from dead ends until a single tube links the food. It is neither a fungus nor an animal.

claims.text: The slime mould Physarum polycephalum has been shown to find a path through a maze to connect food sources.
Sea sponges, coral polyps and sea anemones have not been shown to find their way through mazes.
In maze experiments, the slime mould spread through the corridors and then withdrew from dead ends, leaving a tube along a path that linked the food.
Slime moulds are neither fungi nor animals.

evidence.restatement: The slime mould Physarum polycephalum found a path through a maze to link two food sources (Nakagaki and colleagues, 2000).
No maze-solving has been shown for sea sponges, coral polyps or sea anemones.
The slime mould filled the maze, then withdrew from dead ends, leaving a tube along a route between the food.
Slime moulds are amoebozoans, neither fungi nor animals.
